Got the chance of running the examples and glance over the code... it looks incredibly elegant and clean. Almost feels like this could make engine development fun again.
MIT License, well done! It's so refreshing to see things released with no strings attached... not have to worry about intricacies of GPL etc.
This is amazing. Seriously: I had a look at nearly every game engine/GUI solution in Rust and this is by far the most thought out, ergonomic and complete thing I found.
Having spent a good deal of time working in a dogmatic data driven entity component system similar to this one... it's not necessarily more productive or pleasant than a more conventional approach.
I'm getting security warnings visiting the site, on both Firefox and Chrome... 'Error code: SEC_ERROR_UNKNOWN_ISSUER' on FF at least.
Everything is beautiful so far, the website is nice looking, the overview is self-explanatory... I think one thing that would sell this would be an editor like Godot has.
The integrated code editor in Godot is actually something I don't like... I hope that Bevy users won't be forced to use the Bevy editor for coding.
Bevy's release notes are consistently the best I've ever seen.
It looks great in a lot of respects, but I can't help but notice the aliasing... my screen not being full of moving, weird, and distracting grainy patterns.
Things have started to stabilize, but unless you're willing to get your hands dirty and deal with regular breaking changes, I don't yet recommend staking your livelihood on it.
We support low-end devices well... Bevy runs well on iOS currently... Fans spinning is a known issue, but it is generally decoupled from framerates.
Not sure if there are now well known solutions to get highly defined shadows... model projected shadows are very jagged or really low-res, reminds me of early Unity shadows.
Very cool!! On the last update 0.10 -> 0.11, I had to make quite a few changes on my app, but this time it compiled out of the box!
I'm put off by the limited docs. I've read the Bevy book, only takes a few minutes, and just like that I'm out of resources to turn to when I get stuck.

I've been building a game in Bevy for a while now... UI system was too verbose to comfortably build widgets. Swapped to using egui, but expect to go back to native Bevy within a year. egui has significant limitations, too.

Parent/Child relationships don't have a ton of support (ECS sort-of discourages). It was tougher than expected to associate a label with a sprite, move/rotate it, and keep label following position without following rotation.

Pros have been: Very nice to work in Rust engine + Rust game... Once you get your brain thinking ECS it's tough to go back, feels very flexible (maybe too flexible). Very lively community... Lots of examples (not a lot of docs, but a lot of examples).
Bevy is one of my favorite game engines, especially for larger projects. Asset V2 preprocessing and .meta files look super useful.
Something delightful about this update: it has a lot of new features, some very early, but all by different authors. Seems like such a community effort compared to most early-stage projects.
For my use case, Bevy web (and mobile is nice too) support would mean switching from Godot, 100%.
